questions.questionText: Lens power is measured in:
questions.explanation: Lens power P = 1/f (m) = dioptres. Shorter focal length = higher power.

questions.questionText: How does the human eye focus on objects at different distances?

options.label: A
options.text: By changing the shape of the lens (accommodation)

questions.explanation: Ciliary muscles change lens shape → focal length changes → light focuses on retina.

questions.questionText: Calculate resistance: 12 V across 4 A.
questions.explanation: Ohm's Law states that the current I flowing through a conductor is directly proportional to the voltage V across it, with the constant of proportionality being 1/R, where R is the resistance. Formula: V = I x R, where V is in volts, I in amperes, R in ohms.

questions.questionText: Two resistors (5 Ω and 10 Ω) in series total =:
questions.explanation: Series: R_total = R₁ + R₂ = 5 + 10 = 15 Ω.

questions.questionText: Two 10 Ω resistors in parallel total resistance =:
An electric kettle runs at 240 V and draws 8 A. Power =:
A 2 kW kettle used for 3 hours consumes:
questions.explanation: Electrical energy consumed E = P x t (in watt-hours or kilowatt-hours). 1 kWh = 3.6 x 10⁶ J = 1 unit on the electricity bill. Cost = Energy (kWh) x rate per unit. For example, a 100 W bulb running 10 hours uses 1 kWh of energy.

questions.questionText: Calculate heat dissipated per second in a 10 Ω resistor with 2 A current.
questions.explanation: Electrical power dissipated in a resistor can be calculated using P = VI = I^2R = V^2/R. For a 10 Ω resistor with 2 A current flowing through it: P = I^2R = 4 x 10 = 40 W. This electrical energy is converted to heat (Joule heating).

questions.questionText: Outside a bar magnet, magnetic field lines go from:
questions.explanation: Outside magnet: field lines emerge from N, return to S (in closed loops).
questions.subtopic: Magnet field lines north to south

questions.questionText: Two north poles of bar magnets held close to each other will:
questions.explanation: Like poles repel; unlike poles attract.
questions.subtopic: Magnet like poles repel unlike attract

questions.questionText: A long straight wire carrying current produces a magnetic field that:

options.label: A
options.text: Forms concentric circles around the wire (right-hand grip rule)

options.label: B
options.text: Forms straight lines parallel to wire

questions.explanation: Right-hand grip rule: thumb = current direction; fingers curl = field direction (concentric circles).
questions.subtopic: Magnetic field strength around current wire

questions.questionText: A solenoid carrying current acts like:

options.label: A
options.text: A bar magnet (with N and S poles depending on current direction)

questions.explanation: Solenoid = electromagnet; field similar to bar magnet (N at one end, S at other).
questions.subtopic: Solenoid magnetic field bar magnet equivalent

questions.questionText: Electromagnetic induction was discovered by:
questions.explanation: Faraday (1831) discovered electromagnetic induction (changing magnetic flux induces EMF).

questions.questionText: For electromagnetic induction to occur, the magnetic flux through a coil must:

options.label: A
options.text: Change (change in B, area, or angle)

questions.explanation: Changing flux = changing magnetic field × area × cos θ. Induced EMF requires dΦ/dt ≠ 0.

questions.questionText: Lenz's law states that the direction of induced current:

options.label: A
options.text: Opposes the change that produced it

questions.explanation: Lenz's law = induced current creates magnetic field opposing the original flux change.

questions.questionText: An AC generator is based on:

options.label: A
options.text: Electromagnetic induction (rotating coil in magnetic field)

questions.explanation: AC generator: coil rotates in magnetic field → flux changes → EMF induced → alternating current.

questions.questionText: Three resistors of 4 Ω, 6 Ω and 12 Ω are connected in series. What is the total resistance of the circuit?
questions.explanation: For resistors in series, the total resistance is the sum: R_total = R₁ + R₂ + R₃ = 4 + 6 + 12 = 22 Ω. In series, the same current flows through each resistor, and the voltage divides across them.

questions.questionText: Which of the following best describes how an electromagnet is made?

options.label: A
options.text: By wrapping a coil of insulated wire around a soft iron core and passing a direct current through it

options.label: B
options.text: By hammering a steel bar while it is heated until red hot

options.label: C
options.text: By stroking a piece of soft iron repeatedly with a bar magnet in the same direction

options.label: D
options.text: By placing a permanent magnet inside a hollow plastic tube

questions.explanation: An electromagnet consists of a coil of insulated wire (solenoid) wrapped around a soft iron core. When current flows through the coil, the iron becomes magnetised. Switching off the current removes the magnetism, making it a temporary magnet (unlike a permanent magnet).

questions.questionText: A DC motor works because:

options.label: A
options.text: Current in coil in magnetic field experiences force (turning effect)

questions.explanation: F = BIL; current in coil in B-field → force on each side → couple/rotation (motor effect).
questions.subtopic: DC motor principle current in field

questions.questionText: A fuse wire is rated '5 A'. This means:

options.label: A
options.text: It melts when current exceeds 5 A (protecting circuit)

questions.explanation: Fuse melts if current > rating → opens circuit → protects appliances/wiring.

questions.questionText: Which colour indicates the earth wire in a Malaysian 3-pin mains plug?
questions.explanation: Earth wire = yellow-green stripes. Live = brown. Neutral = blue (Malaysia standard).
questions.subtopic: Live neutral earth wire colours in plug

questions.questionText: The live wire colour in modern Malaysian mains plug wiring is:
questions.explanation: Brown = live (L), Blue = neutral (N), Green/yellow stripes = earth (E).
questions.subtopic: Live wire brown colour UK Malaysia

questions.questionText: Why do some appliances have a 'double insulation' symbol and no earth wire?

options.label: A
options.text: Internal + external insulation prevents user contact with live parts

questions.explanation: Double insulation = two layers; even if one fails, second protects. No earth needed.
questions.subtopic: Double insulation symbol no earth needed

questions.questionText: Why is electrical power transmitted at high voltage over long distances?

options.label: A
options.text: Lower current reduces I²R power loss in cables

options.label: B
options.text: High voltage is cheaper to make

questions.explanation: P_loss = I²R; high V → low I → less heat loss in cables. Transformers step up at generation.
questions.subtopic: Power transmission high voltage reduce loss

questions.questionText: A loudspeaker operates on the principle of:

options.label: A
options.text: Current-carrying coil in magnetic field experiencing force (vibrates cone)

questions.explanation: Coil attached to cone in magnetic field → AC current → varying force → vibration → sound.

questions.questionText: Using the right-hand grip rule for a solenoid, fingers curl in the direction of:
questions.explanation: Right-hand grip: fingers curl = current direction; thumb points = N pole / field direction.

questions.questionText: Why does Lenz's law demonstrate conservation of energy?

options.label: A
options.text: Without opposition, induced current would create free energy (impossible)

questions.explanation: If Lenz's law didn't hold (no opposition), mechanical work → electric energy would violate conservation.

questions.questionText: Which is a hard magnetic material suitable for permanent magnets?
questions.explanation: Steel = hard magnetic material (high retentivity); keeps magnetisation. Soft iron = temporary magnet.

questions.questionText: In a DC motor, 'back EMF' opposes the applied voltage. This results in:

options.label: A
options.text: Lower current after initial surge (limiting current)

questions.explanation: Spinning motor generates back EMF → opposes supply → reduces current draw (limits heat).

questions.questionText: Before electricity enters homes, transformers are used to:

options.label: A
options.text: Step down high voltage to safe 240V household supply

questions.explanation: Step-down transformers near homes reduce transmission voltage (e.g., 11 kV) to 240V.
questions.subtopic: National grid transformer step down use

questions.questionText: Fleming's left-hand rule shows direction of:

options.label: A
options.text: Force on current-carrying conductor in magnetic field (motor effect)

questions.explanation: Left-hand rule: First finger = Field (B), Second finger = Current (I), Thumb = Force/motion (F).

questions.questionText: Fleming's right-hand rule shows direction of:

options.label: A
options.text: Induced current in a moving conductor (generator effect)

questions.explanation: Right-hand rule: First finger = Field (B), Thumb = Motion (v), Second finger = Induced current.

questions.questionText: What does a diode do in a circuit?

options.label: A
options.text: Allows current in one direction only

questions.explanation: Diode = one-way valve for current (forward biased = conducts; reverse biased = blocks).
questions.subtopic: Diode allows current one direction only

questions.questionText: In a simple electric motor, what is the function of the split-ring commutator?

options.label: A
options.text: It reverses the direction of current in the coil every half-turn so the coil rotates continuously

options.label: B
options.text: It increases the magnetic field strength of the permanent magnets

options.label: C
options.text: It converts alternating current (AC) to direct current (DC) for the household supply

options.label: D
options.text: It measures the voltage produced across the rotating coil

questions.explanation: The split-ring commutator in a DC motor reverses the current direction in the coil every half turn. This ensures that the torque on the coil always acts in the same rotational direction, allowing continuous rotation instead of oscillation.

questions.questionText: A NOT gate (inverter) has what logic function?
questions.explanation: NOT gate = inverter. Input 0 → output 1; input 1 → output 0.

questions.questionText: For an AND gate with inputs A=1 and B=1, output =:
questions.explanation: AND: output 1 only if all inputs 1. (1,1) → 1.

questions.questionText: For an OR gate, when is output 1?

options.label: A
options.text: When ANY input is 1 (at least one)

questions.explanation: OR: output 1 if any input is 1 (1 OR 0 = 1; 0 OR 0 = 0).

questions.questionText: Where is most of the mass of an atom concentrated?
questions.explanation: Nucleus contains protons + neutrons → >99.9% of atom's mass (electrons negligible).

questions.questionText: Which particle has a positive charge?
questions.explanation: Proton = +1 charge. Neutron = 0. Electron = −1.

questions.questionText: In the notation ²³⁵₉₂U, the numbers mean:

options.label: A
options.text: Mass number 235 = p + n; atomic number 92 = protons

questions.explanation: A (top) = mass number (p+n). Z (bottom) = atomic number (protons = electrons in neutral atom).
questions.subtopic: Atomic notation A and Z meaning

questions.questionText: How is the carbon-14 isotope written?
questions.explanation: ¹⁴₆C: A = 14 (6p + 8n), Z = 6 (6 protons = carbon).

questions.questionText: Which of the following is a fossil fuel commonly used for generating electricity in power stations?
questions.explanation: Coal is a fossil fuel formed from the remains of ancient plants compressed over millions of years. Other fossil fuels include petroleum (oil) and natural gas. Solar, wind and geothermal are renewable energy sources (not fossil fuels).

questions.questionText: What is an alpha particle?
questions.explanation: α particle = ⁴₂He²⁺ nucleus (2 protons + 2 neutrons).

questions.questionText: What is a beta particle (β⁻)?

options.label: A
options.text: A high-speed electron emitted from nucleus (neutron → proton + electron)

questions.explanation: β⁻ = electron. Neutron converts → proton + electron (+ antineutrino).

questions.questionText: What is a gamma ray (γ)?
questions.explanation: γ = high-energy photon (EM radiation, no mass, no charge), often accompanies α/β decay.

questions.questionText: In α (alpha) decay, the atomic number (Z) changes by:
questions.explanation: α decay loses 2 protons → Z reduces by 2; A reduces by 4.
questions.subtopic: Alpha decay change in atomic number

questions.questionText: In β⁻ (beta-minus) decay, the atomic number (Z) changes by:
questions.explanation: β⁻ decay: neutron → proton + e⁻. So Z (protons) increases by 1. A unchanged.

questions.questionText: In a nuclear power station, the energy released during nuclear fission comes primarily from:

options.label: A
options.text: Conversion of a small amount of mass into a large amount of energy (E=mc^2)

options.label: B
options.text: Combustion of uranium with oxygen releasing heat

options.label: C
options.text: Burning of coal mixed with radioactive uranium ore

options.label: D
options.text: Chemical reaction between U-235 atoms and water

questions.explanation: Nuclear fission of uranium-235 (or plutonium-239) splits the nucleus into smaller fragments, releasing energy according to Einstein's mass-energy equation E=mc^2. A tiny amount of mass is converted into a huge amount of energy (heat), which boils water to drive turbines.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is an advantage of using solar energy compared to fossil fuels?

options.label: A
options.text: Solar energy is renewable and does not produce carbon dioxide during operation

options.label: B
options.text: Solar energy is cheaper to install than coal-fired power plants

options.label: C
options.text: Solar energy can generate electricity 24 hours a day regardless of weather

options.label: D
options.text: Solar panels are made entirely from non-metallic materials

questions.explanation: Solar energy is a renewable resource (sunlight is essentially inexhaustible on human timescales) and generates electricity without emitting CO₂ (a greenhouse gas) during operation. Fossil fuels release CO₂ when burned, contributing to climate change.

questions.questionText: Carbon-14 dating is used to determine:
questions.explanation: C-14 dating: organic materials up to 50,000 years old. Rocks use K-Ar or U-Pb dating.

questions.questionText: How is carbon-14 produced naturally in the atmosphere?

options.label: A
options.text: Cosmic rays collide with nitrogen → C-14 in upper atmosphere

questions.explanation: Cosmic ray neutrons + N-14 → C-14 + proton. C-14 enters biosphere via CO₂ uptake.

questions.questionText: Nuclear fission involves:

options.label: A
options.text: Splitting of a heavy nucleus into smaller fragments + energy

questions.explanation: Fission: heavy nucleus (e.g., U-235) absorbs neutron → splits into lighter fragments + energy + more neutrons.
questions.subtopic: Nuclear fission heavy nucleus split uranium

questions.questionText: Nuclear fusion occurs when:

options.label: A
options.text: Two light nuclei join to form a heavier nucleus + energy

questions.explanation: Fusion: light nuclei combine (e.g., hydrogen → helium in Sun) → releases huge energy.
questions.subtopic: Nuclear fusion light nuclei join helium

questions.questionText: In a nuclear chain reaction, the role of neutrons is to:
questions.explanation: Each fission releases neutrons → which cause more fission → chain reaction (controlled = reactor).

questions.questionText: Control rods in a nuclear reactor absorb excess neutrons to:
questions.explanation: Control rods (boron, cadmium) absorb neutrons → moderate chain reaction → prevent runaway.
questions.subtopic: Nuclear reactor control rods boron cadmium

questions.questionText: What is the role of a moderator in a nuclear reactor?

options.label: A
options.text: Slow down fast neutrons to increase fission efficiency

questions.explanation: Moderator (graphite, water) slows fast neutrons → thermal neutrons → better fission probability.

questions.questionText: Which is NOT a source of background radiation?
questions.explanation: Background radiation: cosmic rays, terrestrial (radon), food, medical. Not mobile phones (ionising vs non-ionising).

questions.questionText: Iodine-131 is used in medicine to:
questions.explanation: I-131 concentrates in thyroid → diagnosis/treatment of thyroid disorders (Goitre, cancer).

questions.questionText: Americium-241 in smoke detectors works by:

options.label: A
options.text: Ionising smoke particles to detect fire

questions.explanation: Am-241 ionises air in chamber → current flows. Smoke disrupts → alarm triggered.

questions.questionText: The Sun's energy comes mainly from:

options.label: A
options.text: Nuclear fusion of hydrogen to helium in its core

questions.explanation: Sun: proton-proton chain → 4 H → He + energy (millions of kelvin required).

questions.questionText: A film badge worn by radiation workers measures:
questions.explanation: Film badge = personal dosimeter; photographic film darkens with radiation exposure → dose measured.

questions.questionText: Which of the following best describes the function of a control rod in a nuclear reactor?

options.label: A
options.text: To absorb excess neutrons and slow down or stop the nuclear chain reaction

options.label: B
options.text: To reflect neutrons back into the reactor core to increase efficiency

options.label: C
options.text: To convert heat energy from fission directly into electrical energy

options.label: D
options.text: To filter radioactive waste products from the coolant water

questions.explanation: Control rods (typically made of boron or cadmium) absorb neutrons in a nuclear reactor. By lowering or raising the rods, the operator controls the rate of the chain reaction. Fully inserted rods stop the reaction (used for shutdown).

questions.questionText: What is the correct order of planets from the sun in our solar system?

options.label: A
options.text: Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, Neptune

questions.explanation: Mercury → Venus → Earth → Mars → Jupiter → Saturn → Uranus → Neptune (from sun).
questions.subtopic: Solar system planets order from sun

questions.questionText: Why is Earth able to support life (unlike other planets)?

options.label: A
options.text: Liquid water, suitable temperature range, atmosphere with oxygen

questions.explanation: Earth: liquid water, moderate T (habitable zone), O₂ atmosphere → supports life.
questions.subtopic: Planet Earth unique liquid water life

questions.questionText: What is the main source of the Sun's energy?

options.label: A
options.text: Nuclear fusion of hydrogen nuclei into helium

questions.explanation: Sun: proton-proton fusion → 4H → He + 2e⁺ + 2ν + energy (E = mc²).
questions.subtopic: Sun source of energy nuclear fusion hydrogen

questions.questionText: In which atmospheric layer does weather occur?
questions.explanation: Troposphere = lowest layer (~0-12 km); contains weather, clouds, water vapour.

questions.questionText: Why is the ozone layer important?

options.label: A
options.text: Absorbs harmful UV radiation from sun

questions.explanation: Ozone (O₃) in stratosphere absorbs UV-B and UV-C → protects life from harmful radiation.

questions.questionText: What causes most earthquakes?

options.label: A
options.text: Movement of tectonic plates at boundaries

questions.explanation: Earthquakes = sudden release of stress at plate boundaries (fault lines).

questions.questionText: Most volcanoes form at:
questions.explanation: Most volcanoes = subduction zones + divergent boundaries (mid-ocean ridges).

questions.questionText: Who proposed the idea of continental drift and Pangaea?
questions.explanation: Wegener (1912): continents once joined as 'Pangaea' and have drifted apart.

questions.questionText: How does Earth's magnetic field protect life?

options.label: A
options.text: Deflects harmful solar charged particles (solar wind)

questions.explanation: Magnetosphere deflects solar wind charged particles → protects atmosphere from being stripped.
questions.subtopic: Earth magnetic field protects solar wind

questions.questionText: A compass needle points north because:

options.label: A
options.text: Earth is a giant magnet (compass aligns with field)

questions.explanation: Compass = small magnet; aligns with Earth's magnetic field (towards magnetic north).
questions.subtopic: Compass needle north Earth magnetic pole

questions.questionText: Which gas is the main contributor to the greenhouse effect?
questions.explanation: CO₂, CH₄, N₂O, water vapour trap infrared → greenhouse effect → global warming.

questions.questionText: What causes day and night on Earth?

options.label: A
options.text: Earth's rotation on its axis (24 hours)

questions.explanation: Earth rotates on its axis every 24 h → day (facing sun) and night (facing away).

questions.questionText: What causes seasons on Earth?

options.label: A
options.text: Earth's axis tilt (23.5°) combined with revolution around sun

questions.explanation: Tilted axis + revolution → varying sun angle and day length → seasons.

questions.questionText: What primarily causes ocean tides?

options.label: A
options.text: Gravitational pull of Moon on Earth (mostly)

questions.explanation: Moon's gravity pulls ocean water → 2 bulges (high tides); Earth rotates → 2 high/low tides/day.

questions.questionText: When do spring tides occur?

options.label: A
options.text: New moon and full moon (Sun, Moon, Earth aligned)

questions.explanation: Spring tides = new/full Moon (Sun + Moon gravity aligned → strongest tides).
questions.subtopic: Spring tide alignment new full moon

questions.questionText: When do neap tides occur?

options.label: A
options.text: First and third quarter moons (Sun/Moon at right angles)

questions.explanation: Neap tides = first/third quarter moons (Sun vs Moon gravity partially cancel).

questions.questionText: Galileo discovered 4 moons orbiting which planet?
questions.explanation: Galileo (1610) discovered 4 largest moons of Jupiter (Io, Europa, Ganymede, Callisto).

questions.questionText: The asteroid belt is located between:
questions.explanation: Asteroid belt between Mars and Jupiter orbits (remnants of planet formation).
questions.subtopic: Asteroid belt location between Mars Jupiter

questions.questionText: What does one light-year measure?

options.label: A
options.text: Distance light travels in one year (~9.46 × 10¹² km)

questions.explanation: 1 light-year = distance light travels in 1 year ≈ 9.46 × 10¹² km (used for astronomy).

questions.questionText: Our Sun is currently in which stage of its life cycle?
questions.explanation: Sun = main sequence star (H fuses to He). Will become red giant in ~5 billion years.
questions.subtopic: Star life cycle main sequence sun

questions.questionText: The Big Bang theory explains:

options.label: A
options.text: Origin and expansion of the universe ~13.8 billion years ago

questions.explanation: Big Bang: universe began as extremely dense/hot point ~13.8 Ga, expanding ever since.
questions.subtopic: Big Bang theory universe expansion origin

questions.questionText: The Hertzsprung-Russell diagram plots:
questions.explanation: H-R diagram: stars classified by luminosity (y-axis) and temperature (x-axis).

questions.questionText: What does red-shift of distant galaxies indicate?
questions.explanation: Redshift = wavelength increases → galaxies moving away → universe expanding (Hubble's law).
questions.subtopic: Red shift galaxy expanding universe Hubble

questions.questionText: Why are some telescopes (like Hubble) placed in orbit instead of ground?

options.label: A
options.text: Avoid atmospheric distortion; clearer space images

questions.explanation: Above atmosphere → no air turbulence → sharper images; access to UV/IR blocked by atmosphere.

questions.questionText: The angle of tilt of Earth's rotational axis is approximately:
questions.explanation: Earth's axial tilt = 23.5° → causes seasons.

questions.questionText: How does increasing atmospheric CO₂ contribute to global warming?

options.label: A
options.text: CO₂ traps infrared radiation from Earth surface

questions.explanation: Greenhouse gases (CO₂, CH₄, N₂O) absorb IR → trap heat → global warming.
questions.subtopic: Greenhouse effect carbon dioxide global warming

questions.questionText: Solar cells (photovoltaic panels) work by:

options.label: A
options.text: Converting sunlight directly to electricity using semiconductor

options.label: B
options.text: Converting light to heat to boil water

questions.explanation: PV cells: photons knock electrons free in semiconductor (e.g., Si) → direct current electricity.

questions.questionText: How does a wind turbine generate electricity?

options.label: A
options.text: Wind spins blades → kinetic energy rotates generator

questions.explanation: Wind KE → rotating blades → shaft turns generator → electricity (electromagnetic induction).
questions.subtopic: Wind energy turbine kinetic to electrical

questions.questionText: Tidal energy is generated by:

options.label: A
options.text: Using tidal water flow to drive turbines

questions.explanation: Tidal power: rising/falling tides drive turbines in barrage → renewable electricity.

questions.questionText: Which of these is NOT a fossil fuel?
questions.explanation: Fossil fuels: coal, oil (petroleum), natural gas. Wood is biomass (renewable resource).

questions.questionText: Why are fossil fuels considered contributors to climate change?
questions.explanation: Combustion of fossil fuels (CxHy) + O₂ → CO₂ + H₂O → increases atmospheric CO₂.

questions.questionText: In a typical water treatment plant, which is the correct order of steps?
questions.explanation: Water treatment: sedimentation (settle), filtration (filter), chlorination (disinfect), supply.

questions.questionText: Why is chlorine added to drinking water?
questions.explanation: Chlorination = disinfection; Cl₂ + H₂O → HCl + HClO → HClO kills microbes.

questions.questionText: Which is a primary benefit of recycling?

options.label: A
options.text: Reduces landfill use; conserves natural resources

questions.explanation: Recycling reduces waste in landfill + saves raw materials + energy.

questions.questionText: What is the correct order of the 3Rs (most preferred to least)?
questions.explanation: Most preferred = reduce (use less), then reuse, then recycle (last resort).
questions.subtopic: Three Rs hierarchy reduce reuse recycle

questions.questionText: Your 'carbon footprint' refers to:

options.label: A
options.text: Total greenhouse gases emitted by your daily activities

options.label: C
options.text: The weight of carbon in your body

questions.explanation: Carbon footprint = total CO₂-equivalent emissions from lifestyle (transport, food, energy).

questions.questionText: Penicillin works by:

options.label: A
options.text: Disrupting bacterial cell wall synthesis (kills bacteria)

questions.explanation: Penicillin inhibits cell wall formation → bacteria cannot survive → infection cleared.

questions.questionText: How does a vaccine provide immunity?

options.label: A
options.text: Stimulates immune system to produce antibodies + memory cells

questions.explanation: Vaccine = weakened/inactivated pathogen → triggers immune response → antibody production + memory.

questions.questionText: In bread-making, yeast causes dough to rise by:

options.label: A
options.text: Producing CO₂ gas during fermentation (anaerobic respiration)

questions.explanation: Yeast: C₆H₁₂O₆ → 2C₂H₅OH + 2CO₂ (anaerobic fermentation). CO₂ makes dough rise.

questions.questionText: In a food chain, which organism is always at the start (base)?
questions.explanation: Producers (autotrophs, green plants) form base of food chain via photosynthesis.

questions.questionText: A food web differs from a food chain because:

options.label: A
options.text: It shows multiple interconnected food chains in an ecosystem

questions.explanation: Food web = many interconnected food chains → more realistic ecosystem representation.

questions.questionText: Approximately what percentage of energy is transferred from one trophic level to the next in a food chain?
questions.explanation: Only ~10% of energy transfers up each trophic level; rest lost as heat/movement/waste.

questions.questionText: An example of an endangered species in Malaysia is:
questions.explanation: Malayan tiger is critically endangered (small wild population). Specific conservation focus in Malaysia.

questions.questionText: How does deforestation affect biodiversity?

options.label: A
options.text: Destroys habitats → species lose homes → extinction risk

questions.explanation: Habitat destruction = main cause of biodiversity loss; species can't migrate or adapt quickly.

questions.questionText: Which gas is a major pollutant from car exhausts causing health problems?
questions.explanation: CO from incomplete combustion → binds haemoglobin (200x affinity of O₂) → suffocation.
questions.subtopic: Air pollution primary gas carbon monoxide vehicle

questions.questionText: Why is carbon monoxide (CO) toxic to humans?

options.label: A
options.text: Binds haemoglobin strongly, prevents O₂ transport in blood

questions.explanation: CO + Hb → COHb (carboxyhaemoglobin); prevents O₂ binding → tissue hypoxia → death (high exposure).

questions.questionText: Excess nutrients (fertiliser) in water cause:
questions.explanation: Nutrients + warm water + light → algal bloom → decomposition uses O₂ → fish die (eutrophication).

questions.questionText: Why are some pesticides (e.g., DDT) considered persistent organic pollutants?

options.label: A
options.text: They do not break down easily; accumulate in food chains (bioaccumulation)

options.label: C
options.text: They are only toxic to plants

questions.explanation: POPs = persistent (long-lasting), bioaccumulative (build up in fatty tissues), toxic. DDT famous example.

questions.questionText: In the carbon cycle, which process returns CO₂ to the atmosphere?
questions.explanation: Respiration by all organisms returns CO₂. Combustion of fossil fuels also adds CO₂.

questions.questionText: In the carbon cycle, photosynthesis removes CO₂ from atmosphere by:

options.label: A
options.text: Converting CO₂ + H₂O into glucose + O₂ (using sunlight)

questions.explanation: 6CO₂ + 6H₂O → C₆H₁₂O₆ + 6O₂ (light energy captured by chlorophyll).

questions.questionText: Which food products are produced using fermentation by microorganisms?
questions.explanation: Fermentation by bacteria/yeast → yoghurt, cheese, bread, soy sauce, vinegar, alcohol.

questions.questionText: Ethanol biofuel can be produced by:
questions.explanation: Fermentation of sugarcane/maize by yeast → ethanol → blended with petrol (gasohol).

questions.questionText: Nanotechnology involves structures at the scale of:
questions.explanation: Nano = 10⁻⁹ m. Nanoparticles, nanotubes have unique properties at this scale.

questions.questionText: How is insulin for diabetes produced by biotechnology?

options.label: A
options.text: Insert human insulin gene into bacteria; bacteria produce insulin

questions.explanation: Recombinant DNA technology: human insulin gene → plasmid → E. coli → produces pure insulin.

questions.questionText: One benefit of a pest-resistant genetically modified crop is:
questions.explanation: GM pest-resistant crops = less pesticide spray + less crop loss → higher yield, environmental benefit.

questions.questionText: How does acid rain affect aquatic ecosystems?

options.label: A
options.text: Lowers lake pH; harms fish/amphibians; disrupts food web

questions.explanation: Acid rain (NOₓ, SO₂ → HNO₃, H₂SO₄) drops to water → acidic → fish eggs/species die.
questions.subtopic: Acid rain effect on aquatic ecosystems

questions.questionText: Why does eutrophication eventually kill fish?

options.label: A
options.text: Algae bloom blocks light + decomposition uses dissolved O₂; fish suffocate

options.label: B
options.text: Fish eat algae and get sick

questions.explanation: Algae cover → less light → plants die → bacteria decompose them → deplete O₂ → fish suffocate.

questions.questionText: Sustainable development aims to balance:

options.label: A
options.text: Economic growth, environmental protection, social well-being

questions.explanation: Sustainability = meeting present needs without compromising future generations (3 pillars).
questions.subtopic: Sustainable development basic triple bottom line

questions.questionText: How does a catalytic converter reduce car exhaust pollution?

options.label: A
options.text: Converts harmful gases (CO, NOₓ) to less harmful (CO₂, N₂, H₂O)

questions.explanation: Catalytic converter: catalysts (Pt, Pd, Rh) speed up oxidation/reduction of pollutants to harmless gases.
questions.subtopic: Catalytic converter vehicle exhaust pollution reduction

questions.questionText: First-aid treatment for CO poisoning includes:

options.label: A
options.text: Move to fresh air, seek medical attention, possibly oxygen

questions.explanation: Move victim to fresh air → oxygen therapy → hospital. CO has 200x affinity for Hb.
questions.subtopic: Carbon monoxide haemoglobin treatment fresh air

questions.questionText: Why is tetraethyl lead (TEL) no longer added to most petrol?

options.label: A
options.text: Toxic to humans; damages catalytic converters; cause lead pollution

questions.explanation: TEL (leaded petrol) = toxic, neurotoxic, ruins catalytic converters → phased out globally.

questions.questionText: Which method does NOT purify drinking water?

options.label: A
options.text: Adding chlorine is needed only for disinfection

questions.explanation: Standing water does NOT purify - just settles particles. Boiling, filtration, chlorination all purify.
questions.subtopic: Water filter ceramic versus activated carbon chlorine

questions.questionText: How does plastic pollution in oceans affect marine wildlife?

options.label: A
options.text: Animals ingest plastic; become entangled; can die

questions.explanation: Sea turtles mistake plastic bags for jellyfish → eat; seals entangled in plastic rings → injury/death.

questions.questionText: Why are heavy metals like mercury considered serious pollutants?
questions.explanation: Heavy metals (Pb, Hg, Cd) = persistent, bioaccumulative, toxic → biomagnification up food chains.

questions.questionText: What is biological magnification (biomagnification)?

options.label: A
options.text: Toxin concentration increases up the food chain

questions.explanation: Biomagnification: persistent toxin (e.g., DDT) accumulates → higher concentration in predators at top.

questions.questionText: How did CFCs (chlorofluorocarbons) damage the ozone layer?

options.label: A
options.text: CFC releases Cl atoms; Cl catalyses O₃ destruction

questions.explanation: CFC + UV → Cl· + other; Cl· + O₃ → ClO + O₂; ClO + O → Cl· + O₂ (chain).

questions.questionText: The Montreal Protocol (1987) addressed which environmental issue?
questions.explanation: Montreal Protocol = international treaty to phase out CFCs/ozone-depleting substances.
questions.subtopic: Montreal Protocol CFC ban international treaty

questions.questionText: Why are fossil fuels called non-renewable?

options.label: A
options.text: They take millions of years to form; cannot be replaced once used

questions.explanation: Non-renewable = used faster than formed (millions of years for fossil fuels; rate of use depletes reserves).

questions.questionText: Renewable resources are those that:

options.label: A
options.text: Can be replenished naturally within a human lifetime

options.label: B
options.text: Never run out regardless of use

questions.explanation: Renewable = replaced by natural processes faster than consumed (e.g., solar, wind, biomass, hydropower).

questions.questionText: An ethical concern of genetic engineering is:

options.label: A
options.text: Potential misuse, designer babies, modified ecosystems

questions.explanation: Ethical concerns: GM impact on ecosystems, biodiversity loss, access inequality, 'designer babies' ethics.

questions.questionText: What is a biodegradable material?

options.label: A
options.text: Material that decomposes naturally by microorganisms

questions.explanation: Biodegradable = broken down by bacteria/fungi naturally (e.g., paper, food waste, some bioplastics).

questions.questionText: In sewage treatment, the secondary stage uses:

options.label: A
options.text: Bacteria to break down organic matter (biological filter)

questions.explanation: Secondary treatment: aerobic bacteria decompose organic matter in activated sludge/trickling filters.

questions.questionText: Composting kitchen waste is an example of:
questions.explanation: Composting = biological decomposition of organic waste → nutrient-rich soil amendment.

questions.questionText: Which is an example of green technology in everyday life?
questions.explanation: Solar panels = renewable energy generation = green technology example.

questions.questionText: What is a 'carbon offset'?

options.label: A
options.text: Compensating for emissions by funding projects that reduce/remove CO₂

questions.explanation: Carbon offset = paying for emissions reduction elsewhere (e.g., tree planting, renewable projects).

questions.questionText: Lead (Pb) in petrol causes health problems including:

options.label: A
options.text: Cognitive impairment in children; nervous system damage

questions.explanation: Pb is neurotoxic: damages developing brains in children → lower IQ, behavioural issues.
questions.subtopic: Lead petrol effect children cognitive impairment

questions.questionText: How does light pollution affect nocturnal wildlife?
questions.explanation: Artificial light disorients nocturnal animals (insects, birds, sea turtles) → disrupts ecosystems.

questions.questionText: Noise pollution affects wildlife by:
questions.explanation: Anthropogenic noise interferes with animal calls (mating, predator detection) → ecological harm.

questions.questionText: What is the purpose of an Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA)?

options.label: A
options.text: To evaluate potential environmental damage before development

questions.explanation: EIA = study to predict + assess environmental effects before project approval (e.g., new highway, factory).

questions.questionText: Which action best demonstrates a 'green consumer' choice?

options.label: B
options.text: Always buying cheapest regardless of packaging

questions.explanation: Green consumer = chooses eco-friendly products, reusable, less packaged, local/sustainable.

questions.questionText: Tay-Sachs disease is caused by deficiency of a specific enzyme in:
questions.explanation: Tay-Sachs = lysosomal hexosaminidase A deficiency → lipid accumulation → neurodegeneration.
questions.subtopic: Lysosome Tay Sachs disease lipid storage

questions.questionText: Which pattern of inheritance suggests mitochondrial DNA mutation?

options.label: A
options.text: Only affected children of affected mothers (not fathers)

questions.explanation: Mitochondrial inheritance = mother only (sperm mitochondria destroyed).

questions.questionText: An example of a polygenic (many-gene) trait in humans is:
questions.explanation: Polygenic traits (height, skin colour, IQ) = many genes + environment.

questions.questionText: Pleiotropy describes:
questions.explanation: Pleiotropy = one gene → multiple phenotypic effects (e.g., sickle cell = anaemia + resistance to malaria).
questions.subtopic: Pleiotropy single gene multiple traits example

questions.questionText: Why is the genetic code said to be 'degenerate'?

options.label: A
options.text: Multiple codons can code for the same amino acid

options.label: B
options.text: Each amino acid has only one codon

options.label: C
options.text: Each codon codes for multiple amino acids

questions.explanation: Degenerate = 64 codons, only 20 amino acids; multiple codons per aa (e.g., UUU & UUC = Phe).
questions.subtopic: Codon degeneracy multiple codons same amino acid

questions.questionText: What is a null hypothesis (H₀) in a scientific experiment?

options.label: A
options.text: Statement of no effect/no difference to be tested

questions.explanation: Null H₀ = no significant effect/difference. Alternative Hₐ = there IS an effect.

questions.questionText: In an experiment investigating how light affects plant height, what is the dependent variable?
questions.explanation: Dependent variable = measured outcome (height). Independent = manipulated (light). Controlled = kept same.

questions.questionText: Why is repeating an experiment (replication) important?

options.label: A
options.text: Confirms reliability; reduces random error chance

questions.explanation: Replication = verify results are reliable + not due to chance.

questions.questionText: Standard deviation measures:

options.label: A
options.text: The average spread of data around the mean

questions.explanation: Standard deviation σ = measure of dispersion around mean. Larger σ = wider spread.

questions.questionText: Reliable measurements are those that:
questions.explanation: Reliable = consistent/reproducible. Valid = measure what intended.

questions.questionText: An experiment is valid if it:

options.label: A
options.text: Tests what it claims to test (no confounding variables)

questions.explanation: Validity = accurate measurement of intended variable; controls confounders.

questions.questionText: What is a histogram useful for showing?
questions.explanation: Histogram = bars touching, for continuous data (intervals).

questions.questionText: Which is an example of discrete data?

options.label: A
options.text: Number of students in a class

questions.explanation: Discrete = counted (whole numbers). Continuous = measured (any value).

questions.questionText: A testable hypothesis must be:
questions.explanation: Falsifiable hypothesis = testable. Can be supported or rejected by data.

questions.questionText: What is the purpose of a pilot study?

options.label: A
options.text: Small-scale test to refine methods before full experiment

questions.explanation: Pilot = small preliminary trial → identify problems, refine procedure → then run full study.
questions.subtopic: Pilot study small scale preliminary test

questions.questionText: Express 0.000045 in scientific notation.
questions.explanation: 0.000045 = 4.5 × 10⁻⁵ (move decimal 5 places right).

questions.questionText: How many significant figures does 0.00340 have?
questions.explanation: Leading zeros not significant. Trailing zeros after decimal are significant. So 3,4,0 = 3 sf.

questions.questionText: The equation v² = u² + 2as. What are the dimensions of 2as?
questions.explanation: a [m/s²] × s [m] = m²/s². So 2as has units of (m/s)² = m²/s². Velocity squared = m²/s².

questions.questionText: A vernier caliper typically measures to a precision of:
questions.explanation: Vernier caliper = 0.01 cm precision (micrometer screw gauge = 0.001 cm / 0.01 mm).

questions.questionText: A micrometer screw gauge typically measures to a precision of:
questions.explanation: Micrometer = 0.01 mm precision (more precise than vernier 0.1 mm).

questions.questionText: A stopwatch typically measures to 0.01 s. What event has duration in this range?
questions.explanation: 100 m race ≈ 10-13 s; stopwatch 0.01 s reads 10.23 s. Earth rotation too long; light too fast.

questions.questionText: Convert 5 km/h to m/s.
If a 50 cm measurement has 0.5 cm uncertainty, the percentage error is:
questions.explanation: % error = (uncertainty / measured value) × 100 = (0.5 / 50) × 100 = 1%.

questions.questionText: Which statement correctly distinguishes distance from displacement?

options.label: A
options.text: Distance is a scalar; displacement is a vector

questions.explanation: Distance = total path length (scalar). Displacement = net change in position (vector).

questions.questionText: Which of these is a physical quantity that has both magnitude and direction (i.e., a vector)?
questions.explanation: Vector = magnitude + direction. Velocity has both. Speed is magnitude only.

questions.questionText: Why does an antacid tablet relieve heartburn?
questions.explanation: Antacid = weak base (Mg(OH)₂, Al(OH)₃); neutralises HCl in stomach → raises pH → relief.

questions.questionText: In the chlor-alkali process, NaOH is produced because:

options.label: A
options.text: OH⁻ remains after H⁺ discharged at cathode (and Cl⁻ at anode)

questions.explanation: Na⁺ + OH⁻ remain in solution (after H₂ + Cl₂ released) → NaOH solution for soap making etc.
questions.subtopic: Brine electrolysis product soap making NaOH

questions.questionText: Litmus paper is made from:
questions.explanation: Litmus = vegetable dye from lichens (e.g., Roccella tinctoria) + absorbed on paper.
questions.subtopic: Litmus natural indicator lichen plant source

questions.questionText: What is concentration of a solution with 0.5 mol of solute in 2 dm³ of solution?
questions.explanation: M = moles / volume = 0.5 / 2 = 0.25 mol/dm³.

questions.questionText: Ammonia (NH₃) is an example of:
questions.explanation: NH₃ + H₂O ⇌ NH₄⁺ + OH⁻ (partial ionisation) = weak base.
questions.subtopic: Weak base ammonia example typical reaction

questions.questionText: An ionic bond typically forms when electronegativity difference exceeds:
questions.explanation: ΔEN > 1.7 → ionic bond (large difference).

questions.questionText: A polar molecule has:
questions.explanation: Polar molecule = permanent net dipole due to polar bonds + shape not cancelling dipoles.

questions.questionText: Why are ionic solids brittle (shatter when struck)?

options.label: A
options.text: Layer shift brings like charges together → repulsion cracks crystal

questions.explanation: Ionic lattice: applied force shifts layers → same-sign ions adjacent → strong repulsion → shatter.

questions.questionText: Van der Waals forces are stronger in molecules that:
questions.explanation: More electrons = more polarisable → stronger temporary dipole → stronger London forces.
questions.subtopic: Van der Waals forces dependence molecular size

questions.questionText: Why is a metal both a good conductor of electricity AND malleable?

options.label: A
options.text: Delocalised electrons allow movement and layer shifting

questions.explanation: Metallic bonding: delocalised e⁻ (mobile, carry current) + layers slide (malleability).

questions.questionText: Absolute zero is the temperature at which:
questions.explanation: 0 K = −273.15°C = theoretical lowest T (no molecular motion, Third Law of Thermodynamics).

questions.questionText: How does CO₂ in the atmosphere contribute to the greenhouse effect?

options.label: A
options.text: Absorbs infrared radiation emitted from Earth surface

questions.explanation: CO₂ absorbs IR radiation from warmed Earth → traps heat → global warming.

questions.questionText: At night, the land breeze blows from:
questions.explanation: Night: land cools faster than sea → cool land air sinks → warmer sea air rises → breeze from land to sea.
questions.subtopic: Land breeze night time direction ocean

questions.questionText: Why does water have a high specific heat capacity?

options.label: A
options.text: Hydrogen bonds require extra energy to break

questions.explanation: H-bonds need extra energy to break/move → water absorbs lots of heat per °C rise.
questions.subtopic: Specific heat capacity water high reason

questions.questionText: Convection cannot occur in a vacuum because:
questions.explanation: Convection requires fluid movement. Vacuum = no medium = no convection.
questions.subtopic: Convection cannot occur in vacuum why

questions.questionText: What are the two most abundant gases in Earth's atmosphere?
questions.explanation: Dry air: ~78% N₂, ~21% O₂, ~1% Ar + trace CO₂, etc.

questions.questionText: How long does the Moon take for one cycle of phases (new moon to new moon)?
questions.explanation: Synodic month (new → new) ≈ 29.5 days = lunar cycle.
questions.subtopic: Moon phases new full quarter lunar cycle

questions.questionText: The Sun is classified as which colour/type on H-R diagram?
questions.explanation: Sun = G2V yellow main sequence star (yellow dwarf).
questions.subtopic: Sun star classification main sequence colour

questions.questionText: GPS satellites orbit Earth primarily to provide:
questions.explanation: GPS = 24+ MEO satellites; triangulate Earth positions for navigation (mobile phones, planes).

questions.questionText: Astronomers measure the distance to nearby stars by:
questions.explanation: Stellar parallax = apparent shift due to Earth's orbit → calculate distance (triangulation).
